finding.expected: Treat authorized_main_sha as immutable historical integration identity, not as a required equality with the current lifecycle main. Continue to validate the exact remote integration ref/id/candidate and its exact parents [cumulative_tip_candidate_sha, authorized_main_sha] through resolve_valid_integration(require_remote=True). Add an explicit chronology regression where a valid integration is created against an older authorized main, then remote main is advanced by one or more canonical commits before observing the integrated REMEDIATION FAILURE. That valid historical RUN must reduce to AUTHOR_REPAIR/EXECUTE_REPAIR. Preserve fail-closed behavior for forged authorized_main_sha by requiring the exact derived remote integration ref/parents, and if an additional current-main relationship is required, use a bounded historical relationship such as authorized_main_sha being an ancestor of current canonical main rather than strict equality.
finding.issue: The integrated REMEDIATION decoder still rejects the real RUN-140-008 chronology after canonical main advances. The new branch requires item.execution_base.authorized_main_sha == lifecycle.main_sha. But authorized_main_sha is the immutable main SHA that was authorized when the integration candidate was created, while lifecycle.main_sha is the current remote main at observation time. RUN-140-008 is bound to integration authorized_main_sha 7b023727b061d3a0bb6c62be27e4387a0b0a6b17, whereas current main has already advanced through TASK-143 authoring to ada501871399247540fd9d7c54279742880214e8. Therefore the exact historical integrated RUN that TASK-143 is intended to recover will still reduce to MALFORMED_CANONICAL_STATE as soon as this decoder observes it. The new regression is not actually equivalent to RUN-140-008 because _setup_divergent_integrated_topology uses the same new_main both as the integration authorized_main_sha and as RemoteTaskLifecycle.main_sha, so it never exercises canonical-main advancement after the integrated RUN was created.
